--- title: "Predicting Eviction Filings in Philadelphia" subtitle: "A Census-Tract Level Negative Binomial Model" author: "Huda, Dalanda, Wesley, Yusuf" date: today format: revealjs: theme: simple slide-number: true transition: fade --- ## Problem & Policy Context Extent literature shows the devastating effects of evictions on health, social, and economic outcomes. Evictions are spatially correlated and persistent over time. A targeted, more focused approach to eviction prevention is important in Philadelphia given that it is the second poorest city in the U.S. There were over **13,000** eviction filings in the past 12 months in the city. Black & female Philadelphians were more likely to receive an eviction threat in the last 12 months than their white and male counterparts, respectively. ## Motivation We create a predictive model for eviction filings to identify areas wherein to target eviction prevention strategies and resources more effectively. ## Research Question Which census tracts in Philadelphia are most at risk of receiving eviction filings? Which variables best predict eviction filings? ## Data Sources - Eviction filings data, 2020–2026 (Eviction Lab) - Census ACS (ACS5, 2022) — income, race, mobility, rent burden, vehicle access - OpenDataPhilly — bike network, landmarks, 311 maintenance complaints - Eviction Lab Top 100 Filers (Philadelphia hotspots) - Census tract boundaries (TIGER/Line) - Our integration approach was joining our data by census tract ## Demographic Overview ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Demographic Overview ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Demographic Overview ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-4-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Where Are Evictions Concentrated? ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Temporal Patterns ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Temporal Patterns ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Methods Overview :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} **Negative Binomial** - Count data - Poisson: overdispersion - Logistic: lose too much detail **Integration Approach** - Joined using GEOID / Census Tract - Unit of analysis: filings by week, month, season ::: ::::{.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Overdispersion Diagnostics
Metric Value
Mean of outcome 0.631
Variance of outcome 1.474
Variance / Mean 2.335
Dispersion (Pearson) 2.295
````` ::: ::: ::: :::: ## Model Building *We built 5 models in sequence* - Model 1: baseline (season + month) - Model 2: + temporal lags - Model 3: + demographics (age, race, income) - Model 4: + rent burden, new residents, transit commuters - Model 5: + physical features (landmarks, bike lanes, maintenance complaints) - Model 6: + top 100 owners who filed evictions in Philadelphia ## Model Performance ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-9-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Spatial Errors ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Error vs Demographics ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-11-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Error vs Season ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Predicted vs Observed ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-13-1.png){width=960} ::: ::: ## Final Model Comparison ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
Each layer prediction improves prediction
Model MAE RMSE
1. Baseline season 0.80 1.17
2. + temporal lags 0.78 1.62
3. + demographics 0.73 1.21
4. + rent burden, mobility, interaction effect 0.73 1.23
5. + landmarks, bike lanes, and maintenance complaints 0.72 1.18
6. + top 100 property owners filing evictions (Final) 0.71 1.16
````` ::: ::: ## Recommendations - Promote intervention program that supports census tracts that have high counts of eviction filings - Conduct outreach and assessment in tracts with high counts of eviction filings - Connect non-profit community organizations with identified census tracts to allocate resources - Investigate top 100 eviction filers ## Limitations and Bias Considerations - Data is aggregated at the tract level, so we miss intra-tract differences - Data captures filings not processed evictions - Eviction rates are higher for Black renters than white renters - Historical inequities shape socioeconomic qualities like income and rent burden - This type of model could be misused to stigmatize poorer and Black neighborhoods ## Questions? Thank you

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
